meaningMnemonic: There are fins wrapped in a towel in winter. Who is drying these fish fins to eat them? A penguin .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means wave .
That penguin over there seems to have a towel stuffed with cash . Hints The towel the cash is in even has a big $ on it like the ones they have at the bank. You follow the penguin into a back alley.
readingMnemonic: Your eyes follow the cash , and you watch as the penguin stuffs it, towel and all, into a hay ( へい ) stack. What a smart penguin, people don't look for cash in hay, they're too busy looking for needles. Hints You wait for the penguin to leave and you run over to the hay stack and stick your hand in. But you don't feel the towel or the cash! Instead you pull out your hand and it's full of hay and needles. Ouch! No fair, gimme that cash!!

meaningMnemonic: You give bamboo to someone and they make them into chopsticks . They are very talented at turning bamboo into bamboo chopsticks. This someone is an expert at their profession. Hints Watch this person take ordinary bamboo and transform it into chopsticks right before your eyes. Hear the whooshing and whittling sounds as they form the bamboo into chopsticks with expert speed and precision.
readingMnemonic: Now use those chopsticks to eat some delicious hash ( はし ) browns! That's what chopsticks were made for. That's what they're always made for. Hints Imagine trying to pick up hash browns with your chopsticks. They would be really hard to eat if you didn't have these handy eating tools!

meaningMnemonic: Rub charcoal under your eye s if you want to see clear ly. Sports players also rub charcoal under their eyes to see nice and clear in the bright sun. Hints You can even rub charcoal in your eyes if you really want to clear them up, but you should probably only do this under the supervision of your eye doctor.
readingMnemonic: You have to have clear vision because you're about to go out in your row ( りょう ) boat. The light off the water shines right into your eyes and you need the charcoal to clear that up for you. Otherwise you'll end up crashing into the shore or going over a waterfall to your death. Hints Imagine how dangerous it would be not to have clear vision while you row around in a row boat. You might even smack yourself in the face with your own oars.

meaningMnemonic: There is a mountain on top of a bunch of dirt with a steep cliff . This is a bit redundant, but the mountain and the dirt just make the cliff even bigger and steeper and scarier. Hints Imagine a cliff. Now add two big helpings of dirt and a mountain to the top. It's still a cliff, it's just more cliff than before.
readingMnemonic: You can't believe how big the cliff is now with the mountain and the dirt. You look at it for so long, you just become another gawker ( がけ ) who can't stop staring at the huge cliff. It really is huge. Hints Imagine a giant cliff that turns every passerby into a gawker, just like you.

meaningMnemonic: Without a fire , you will lack the ability to cook anything. You really need a fire to cook properly. Having a fire will make sure any cooking endeavors you attempt will not fail. Hints Imagine yourself as you cook with a fire very confidently. Knowing you cannot fail, feel the heat and hear the crackling embers of the fire. Smell the delicious smell of whatever you are cooking as well.
readingMnemonic: You cook your meal evenly by swi nging ( すい ) it back and forth over the fire. You swing it left, you swing it right. You swing it to, you swing it fro. All this swinging ensures a properly cooked meal. Hints Imagine swinging this meal over the fire. Feel the flames licking at your fingertips as you cook this meal by swinging it back and forth over the fire.

meaningMnemonic: Sitting safely under your canopy you take rice and dirt , mix it up, and create unique cosmetics for your face. Hints Imagine mixing dirt and rice together to make some cosmetics that best fit your skin tone and type. No one will see you doing it under this canopy too, so the secret formula you come up with will be safe.
readingMnemonic: You need these cosmetics because you have a meeting with the Shou gun ( しょう ) coming up. You want to impress him, and you don't want anyone to copy your look. Hints Imagine meeting the Shougun with your new cosmetics all over your face. You look amazing! Stunning! The shougun wants to know where you got that foundation, you're glowing!

meaningMnemonic: A building falls into the dirt when a pig with horns crash es into it. The building literally crashes to the ground when the horned pig attacks it. Hints Picture a pig with horns crashing into a building and both of them crashing into the dirt. Uh oh, is the pig dead?
readingMnemonic: You pull the poor pig out of the rubble of the crash . It's not dead, but it had a nasty bump to the head and now thinks it's a bird. " TWEE T ( つい )!" says the pig. "Tweet, tweet, tweet!" Poor confused pig. Hints Imagine trying to explain to the pig that it's a pig, and not a bird. "Tweet, tweet, tweet!" says the pig again. Oh dear.

meaningMnemonic: A crab will try to hide what it lack s with deceit . Lying, stealing, faking things—no type of deceit is too much for a crab. Hints Covering things up with deceit is pretty much the worst thing you can do, so don't be like this crab.
readingMnemonic: Deceit can only take you so far, and soon the crab is caught, tried for its crimes and coverups, and sentenced to death via gui llotine ( ぎ ). Hints Picture the crab with its head, er, front half? Whatever, it's in the guillotine and it's screaming, "You've been deceived! I never deceived anyone, you're all sheep!"

meaningMnemonic: What would a door criminal steal? A door , of course, but specifically a hinged door . You know, the kind that swings open and shut? That's the kind of door 扉 means. Hints Imagine waking up one morning to find all your doors missing. The door criminal strikes again! They left the sliding door behind though, since they only wanted the hinged 扉 ones. So… there's that at least?
readingMnemonic: To protect your door , you get help from 飛び Ra ( とびら ). 飛び Ra is the flying ( 飛び ) version of Ra, the Egyptian sun god. Whenever a criminal tries to steal your door, 飛び Ra flies out from behind it and blinds them with his sun-god brightness. Hints Now picture yourself waking up to a bright, beautiful morning with all your 扉 doors still safely attached to their hinges. Thanks, 飛び Ra!

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami hits your mohawk and it begins to drip . The water from the tsunami continues to drip from your mohawk long after the tsunami has passed. There’s a lot of water in your hair now, so it’s probably going to drip for a while. Hints Imagine having all this tsunami water in your hair. Hear it drip from your mohawk. Drip… drip… drip…
readingMnemonic: Luckily, you’re a self-proclaimed techie ( てき ), so you develop a device to stop the drip drip dripping. This techie device of yours is like a hair dryer helmet. You put it over your mohawk, it does its thing, and your hair is dry! Being a techie sure does have its benefits. Hints Feel the weight of this dryer helmet on your head as you listen to it whirr away. The dripping has finally stopped! Success!

meaningMnemonic: In the dirt there are flag s and horns lined up with a lantern attached to them, making a fence . It's a little weird looking, but these things are definitely supposed to fence something in. Hints Can you see the fence made of horns and flags through the light of the lantern?
readingMnemonic: You want to know what this fence is fencing in, so you take a step closer. As the light from the lantern gets brighter you see that the fence is around a ton of hay ( へい ). Hints Picture yourself climbing over this fence (that you're definitely not supposed to climb based on all these flags and horns) and falling into the piles of hay. It's a little scratchy, but otherwise pretty comfy!

meaningMnemonic: It's rain ing on your spear that has winter power . When the warm rain hits your cold, winter spear, it creates fog . Hints When warm water touches a cold spear, fog billows out and covers everything.
readingMnemonic: Through the fog you see the shape of a mythical kiri n ( きり ). You can only see the outline through the fog, but you know it's there. Hints You walk toward the kirin through the fog. When you get close, the image before you becomes clear: it's two cans of Kirin beer on a slide. Next time you see fog, keep your eyes peeled for the real kirin in the kiri.

meaningMnemonic: After passing through a door , you use a feather to put the finishing touches on a folding fan . The door leads to your folding fan workshop where you make all your folding fans. This folding fan is now complete that you’ve added a feather to it. How lovely it is. Hints Use this folding fan to fan your face. Feel the refreshing breeze as you admire the gorgeous feather you just added. What a fashionista you’ve become.
readingMnemonic: Your biggest folding fan customer is a cen taur ( せん ). This centaur just loves your folding fans and this one you just made with the feather was for the centaur’s latest order. You go back out your door and deliver this folding fan to the centaur. Hints Imagine handing this newly made folding fan to the centaur. See his face light up with delight as he examines your fine craftsmanship and starts fanning himself with it. Another satisfied customer!

meaningMnemonic: A soul will only inhabit a root if it's holding a grudge . Have you ever seen a nice, haunted tree? No! They're always angry and trying to get someone back for something. Hints Don't die with a grudge, or your soul might end up angry and trapped in some roots.
readingMnemonic: If you see one of these grudge trees, it's probably inhabited by the soul of a con dor ( こん ). Humans tend to kill condors and take their trees away to build houses and make toilet paper. So condors hold pretty bad grudges against us, and so their souls end up stuck in a lot of trees. Hints Picture a tree with the soul of a condor with a grudge in it before you. You feel bad about being so wasteful with paper and chopsticks now, huh?

meaningMnemonic: You take a towel and wrap it around your head to keep the sun out of your eye s. You've invented... the hat ! Hints A hat is just a piece of cloth or a towel you get to stay on your head. Extra points if it protects your eyes from the sun.
readingMnemonic: After inventing the hat , you wanted to show it off to everyone, so you went to the bow ling ( ぼう ) alley. You really stood out bowling strike after strike in your fancy new hat, and before you knew it, people had coined a term for your funky headpiece. That's right — you became the namesake of the iconic bowler hat! Hints Imagine sitting your grandkids on your lap someday and telling them how you're the person the bowler hat's named after. They'll be bursting with pride and admiration.

meaningMnemonic: The soul mask helps you to see the deepest part of anyone's soul. You look around and in all the people you only see hate . Hints You're supposed to see all the emotions, so why do you only see hate inside everyone?
readingMnemonic: It turns out you're not looking at normal people. You see so much hate because all the people you're looking at are actually just a group of zo mbies ( ぞう ). Hints Zombies are pretty filled with hate, so it makes sense that you'd see a bunch of hate if you used the soul mask on them.

meaningMnemonic: The leader of a narwhal construction crew needs all the help he can get. The narwhals are beginning construction on an underwater city. The leader knows the narwhals are hard construction workers, but they’ll need some help building this city. Hints Imagine being the narwhal leader and asking others for help. Ask a shark for help. Ask a whale for help. Ask a shrimp for help. Go on, ask.
readingMnemonic: Then you discover a saw ( さ ) who would be a great big help . This saw is very strong and would help you and your narwhal construction team out a lot. You should make use of this saw right away. Hints Imagine using this saw and realizing how big of a help it is. Hear the saw sawing away as you and your fellow narwhals get to work.

meaningMnemonic: You have fingers in the thousand s and while looking up at the sun you decide you want to insert them in there. Hints Hold your thousand+ fingers up to the sun and imagine inserting them into the sun's super-hot ... s-sun lava. (That's what it is, right? Yeah, let's go with that.)
readingMnemonic: You insert one finger, it burns up immediately, and its sou l ( そう ) comes flying out screaming for a moment before it disappears. Hmm. You insert another finger and as it burns up, another little soul comes out screeching, "WHY WOULD YOU INSERT ME IN THERE!" and is gone. Hints Since you have a thousand fingers too many, you decide to insert them all into the sun and watch as their souls pop out. You listen to the little souls scream at you.

meaningMnemonic: A leader and Wolverine take a slide to Italy . Wolverine’s leader is Professor X, and they are both sliding down a big slide to Italy. How fun! Hints Imagine Wolverine and his leader Professor X going down this slide to Italy. Hear them wooping and cheering as they ride down the slide. Whee~
readingMnemonic: Before Professor X can get off the slide into Italy , a large ea gle ( い ) swoops down and plucks him right out of his wheelchair. That eagle is very strong. Goodbye, Professor X! Hints Imagine this eagle carrying Professor X away from Italy and out over the ocean. You can also remember this reading easily because Italy starts with the letter I. Super simple stuff.

meaningMnemonic: They say the key to telling a lie is to totally believe the lie yourself. They say that if you believe your own lie, others will believe it as well. This is key. Hints Imagine an actual key going from you to another person. This key is the lie. You gotta believe in the lie for it to reach the other person and unlock their understanding. Visualize this visual lie.
readingMnemonic: The lie you told was about not stealing your buddy’s saw ( さ ). You actually did steal his saw. He saw you steal his saw, but now you are trying to lie your way out of it. It’s not going well. Hints Imagine trying to lie your way out of this. He saw you steal his saw. He caught you red handed. What sort of lie can you spin to get yourself out of this situation?

meaningMnemonic: With a woman 's mouth , you have a likeness to me. Hints Imagine someone's putting a woman's mouth over your mouth, looking at you, and commenting on your likeness. All it took was this woman's mouth.
readingMnemonic: You have a likeness to Jo -Anne ( じょ ) when you wear that mouth. Hints Jo-Anne popped her mouth off and put it on you. Indeed with that mouth on, you have an extreme likeness to her.

meaningMnemonic: A landslide came out of your mouth and created your lips . Before the landslide, you just had a wide open mouth hole. Hints Picture your mouth as an open hole. Now a landslide of something (words? food? something worse?) comes pouring out, and when it's done you have lips. You flap them open and closed to test them out.
readingMnemonic: Now you can use your new lips to enjoy a nice, cold Kuchi beer ( くちびる ). The Kuchi people are Afghan Pashtun nomads. They are lesser known for their amazing beer. And you've never been able to get this delicious beer into your mouth, but now that you have lips you can get it all in there. Hints Imagine wrapping your new lips around the mouth of this Kuchi beer bottle. It's so good! And you aren't spilling any of it!

meaningMnemonic: A wave crashes into a woman , transforming her into an old woman ! The wave washes away all of the woman's makeup, revealing her to be an old woman. The makeup she had on made her appear to be a much younger woman, but once the wave washed away her makeup, she was revealed for the old woman she is. Hints Imagine a gorgeous woman. Now see her get hit by a wave of water and turn into an old woman. The old woman could still be pretty too, she just looks way old now. Like ancient.
readingMnemonic: In an attempt to distract you from the fact that she is actually an old woman , the old woman starts to baa ( ば ) and act like a sheep. The old woman goes "Baa! Baa!" and hops around on all fours like a sheep. Hints Imagine this old woman acting like a sheep, just saying "baa" over and over and over again. Baa! Baa! Baa!

meaningMnemonic: If you want to cover a Viking 's mouth with your hand , you have to use your palm . Why the palm? Well, if you do it knuckles-to-mouth, you're sort of just punching the Viking… and you don't want a punch a Viking. That's why you use the palm. Hints And don't use your fingers either, 'cause they'll just get bitten off. You absolutely want to make sure it's the palm — a nice flat open palm. It's a lot like feeding a horse, I guess.
readingMnemonic: This Viking-touching technique of using the palm was developed by the Shou gun ( しょう ). The Shogun has to deal with a lot of loudmouthed Vikings, so he's learned to use his palm to cover their mouths. Hints Imagine if a Shogun and a Viking had actually met in history (never mind that the dates don't overlap). You can definitely picture the quiet, refined Shogun putting his palm over the mouth of some noisy Viking during a tough diplomatic meeting.

meaningMnemonic: With a lid , you hit yourself in the mouth and then kick it like a pathetic loser. You kick the lid, even though it is your fault that you hit yourself in the mouth with it. It’s not the lid’s fault. You don’t need to kick it. You’re being pathetic. Hints Imagine kicking this lid and with each kick you feel a little bit more pathetic. Your mouth hurts a lot too.
readingMnemonic: You kick the lid one last time and it bounces off the wall and hits you in the eye ( あい ). How pathetic . You are a pathetic mess. You should have never kicked the lid. Now both your eye and your mouth are in pain, you pathetic fool, you. Hints Hold your eye with one hand and your mouth with the other. Feel them pulse in pain as you reflect on how pathetic you are today.

meaningMnemonic: An insect specializing in construction builds a rainbow . Did you ever wonder where rainbows come from? Construction insects build them. Construction insects build rainbows. Hints Imagine this insect with a construction hat on, building a rainbow. He works very fast. The resulting rainbow is beautiful!
readingMnemonic: This rainbow building insect is so needy ( にじ ). He is needy because he needs everyone to look at his rainbow and praise him for what he’s done. “Look at my rainbow! Look at how good it is and I am! I’m so needy! Needy for praise and recognition!” Hints Imagine this construction insect being all whiny and needy for attention and stuff. It’s pathetic. Hear him whine and whine because of how needy he is.

meaningMnemonic: A big treasure treasure treasure treasure is refreshing ! Sorry, I can’t say treasure treasure treasure treasure without saying it four times. See? I did it again. Anyway, this big treasure treasure treasure treasure is really refreshing. It’s been a long time since you found a treasure treasure treasure treasure, so finding this big one is really refreshing. Hints Imagine finding this big treasure treasure treasure treasure and being really refreshed and relieved and happy. This treasure treasure treasure treasure is so big, you’ll be set for life!
readingMnemonic: You’d had a sour ( さわ ) taste in your mouth for not being able to find any treasure treasure treasure treasure for such a long time, but now that you found this big one, the sour taste is totally gone and it’s sooooo refreshing ! Hints Imagine the most sour taste you could ever imagine. So super-duper sour! Now imagine that sour taste instantly melting away once you discover this big refreshing treasure treasure treasure treasure. Jackpot!

meaningMnemonic: You keep your tongue to your self to give your heart a rest . You’ve been talking and moving your tongue around all day expressing your feelings. This has tired both your tongue and your heart out, so you stop your tongue moving and decide that you need some self rest time. Hints It's important to let yourself rest every now and then, you know.
readingMnemonic: What better way to rest than to eat some ca ke ( けい )! No talking necessary. Just enjoy the delicious taste of cake on your tongue and feel your heart let out a sigh of relief. Hints You should rest right now. Take a break from Japanese and go eat some cake. (Just remember to come back when your tongue and heart are sufficiently rested!)

meaningMnemonic: If only the front of something gets boil ed, you're going to have to roast it next. Roasting is the best way to cook something all the way through — especially when you've only managed to boil the front of it. Hints You must really be a lousy cook to fail so badly at boiling something. Thankfully, roasting it will be an excellent backup plan.
readingMnemonic: What is it that you're going to roast ? A cen taur ( せん ). Hopefully you've got a pretty big oven to roast this thing in, because centaurs are not small. Hints Imagine trying to jam this centaur into your oven so you can roast it. It was too large to fit in your pot — hence why you only boiled the front of it — but you're confident that you'll get it into your oven somehow.

meaningMnemonic: This shrimp is the exact length of a shaku , or Japanese foot . That’s how they came up with this form of measurement. They measured the length of this shrimp and it was the length of a Japanese foot which they deemed the shaku. It’s equal to 30.3cm, very close to one imperial foot. Hints Imagine this foot long shrimp. It’s pretty big. Imagine it squirming about making a “shaku shaku” sound as it worms about.
readingMnemonic: How is shaku , the Japanese foot , pronounced by Shaq ( しゃく ) in Japanese? Why Shaq pronounces it shaku. It’s pronounced shaku in both English and Japanese. Hints Imagine Shaq dribbling the shrimp like a basketball, saying “shaku, shaku, shaku” every time he bounces the shrimp.

meaningMnemonic: Take this stone and throw it at nine cross es to smash them! It's like old-fashioned bowling, but instead of rolling this stone to knock down the crosses, you want to completely smash them to bits! Hints Picture the nine crosses in front of you, lined up in a triangle. Now take your rock, hold it above your head, and SMASH it down on them as hard as you can!!
readingMnemonic: As you smash these crosses, you think of your cy borg ( さい ) and how much you want to smash the people who took it away from you. Your cyborg was so good at smashing things too. You could be smashing together, if you didn't have to sell it. Hints You smash things because your own heart has been smashed by your cyborg. :'(

meaningMnemonic: Your rice fortune is sticky . Rice is sticky. So is your rice fortune. Your fortune of rice is sticky because it is made up entirely of sticky rice. Hints Look at this sticky rice fortune of yours. Run your hands through it and feel the sticky rice between your fingers. Hear the soft, sticky sound of it as you stir and knead it about.
readingMnemonic: This rice is so sticky that you're able to sculpt nen doroid ( ねん ) figurines from it. Your rice fortune is worth even more now that you're using it to churn out limited edition nendoroids. Hints Imagine sculpting these sticky rice nendoroids with your bare hands. Feel the sticky rice between your fingers as you mold it into the shape of big-headed anime characters.

meaningMnemonic: In the rice paddy there is a forehead with a top hat . It sits atop an area of tatami mat s. Hints The meaning you're trying to learn is tatami mat, so focus on the beautiful tatami mats that are strangely in the middle of this rice paddy. On top is a forehead with a top hat. It almost looks like the tatami mats are an altar for this gruesome scene.
readingMnemonic: Who made this creepy tatami mat altar? It was Joe ( じょう ), the increasingly concerning farmhand who lives in your village. Hints You saw Joe setting up the tatami mats a day earlier, but you thought he was just making an area for workers in the field to rest in. Does the forehead with a top hat have anything to do with Joe? What sort of ominous sign could this be?

meaningMnemonic: The moon is the same as your torso . You must have a really huge torso for it to be the same as the moon. Hints Imagine if your torso was as large as the moon. You’re a gigantic human. Imagine floating around in space like this. Wooooaaaahhh.
readingMnemonic: Your torso got so big because of all the dough nuts ( どう ) you ate. You ate so many doughnuts that your torso got to be the size of the moon and then you floated away into space with your own gravitational pull and everything. Doughnuts are dangerous things. Hints Imagine how many doughnuts you would have to eat to get your torso this size. Now imagine eating all of those doughnuts. I hope you like doughnuts, because you’re going to be eating a lot of them.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the radical are the same, so remembering the meaning of this kanji is as simple as making sure you know the radical for towel first! If you know the radical, you know this kanji means towel as well. Hints Make sure you know those radicals, yo!
readingMnemonic: You know who loves towel s? The Kin g ( きん ) of England. He loves towels so much that he went around and put きん on every towel in the land, so you think of him whenever you use one. Hints Go into your bathroom or your linen closet right now. Look at your towels. Look for the small きん hidden there.

meaningMnemonic: There are flowers growing around a heart with a wick sticking out of it. The heart is a sacrifice to the old gods and the life energy bleeds from the burning wick to feed the flowers. The wick burns, releasing the power of the heart which spreads into the ground around the heart causing the flowers to grow. Hints See this morbid scene. As the wick burns you can smell the smell of burning organs. The flowers are pretty though.
readingMnemonic: Sometimes the wick burning the heart isn’t enough for the flowers to grow properly and they get thirsty for the blood from your shin ( しん ). So, you slice open your shin with a sacrificial knife and drip your blood over the thirsty demon flowers. Hints Imagine slicing your shin with a knife, causing blood to drip on the flowers around the heart with a wick in it. Your shin really hurts from the injury, but the flowers are rejoicing as they’re showered in blood.

meaningMnemonic: A tree that is stamp ed with one pattern, then stamp ed with another pattern, over and over, is the willow tree. Hints A willow tree is a tree that looks like it's on repeat over and over again. It also looks nice on a stamp. Note that the first stamp is kind of an ugly looking backwards stamp, and the second stamp is the normal stamp radical.
readingMnemonic: Ryu ( りゅう ) from Street Fighter really loves willow trees. Ryu loves them so much that he makes out with them. Ryu is open mouth kissing a willow tree. You are watching this. It is happening. Hints Watch Ryu as he French kisses this willow tree. Hear him slurping and moaning in ecstasy. Why are you watching this? This is gross. Wait – is this turning you on!? Ew.

meaningMnemonic: If something sticky wears something else on it, it will stick together because there's adhesion between them. 粘着 refers to the adhesive properties of a material, especially in compound words like 粘着テープ (adhesive tape). On its own, it often describes the behavior of people who can't let go of a particular issue and keep on about it in unwanted ways.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: どうして粘着テープを宝石箱に仕舞っているの？
sentences.english: Why do you keep the adhesive tape in your jewelry box?

meaningMnemonic: A supplement of help is a form of assistance . 補佐 is a formal word for the act of providing support to a leader or person in charge. It can also refer to an official or organizational role, like 部長補佐 (an assistant general manager).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 私はトーフグ営業部の補佐として働きました。
sentences.english: I worked as an assistant in the Tofugu sales department.

meaningMnemonic: Ten thousand year s! That's a lot of time. This is the word for the turned-English Japanese phrase, banzai ! 万歳 is a cheerful word used to shout " hooray !" when celebrating something good. Because it's usually said with both arms raised, the action of raising one's arms can also be referred to as 万歳 . This is often used when talking to children, like when telling them to raise their arms to take off a shirt. And since raising your hands can also mean " I give up " in Japan, 万歳 can sometimes mean that as well. So basically, it's either "Yay, we did it!" or "That's it, I'm done." It really covers all your bases!
readingMnemonic: The reading isn't the same as 万 's normal reading. It's ばん instead of まん . And 歳 gets rendaku'd. But, since the word "banzai" is so well known, you probably can remember this reading: ばんざい ( Hooray )! And if it's too hard and you can't remember, you can still say ばんざい ( I give up ). Basically, you're gonna end up saying ばんざい either way, so you'll remember it eventually… in theory, at least.

sentences.japanese: トフグのコウイチに万歳三唱をしましょう！万歳！万歳！万歳！
sentences.english: Three cheers for Koichi of Tofugu! Hip hip hooray! Hip hip hooray! Hip hip hooray!

meaningMnemonic: If you have a naked foot , it means you're not wearing anything on your foot, making you barefoot .
readingMnemonic: The reading here is a bit weird. It's like the words 裸 ( はだか ) and 足 ( あし ) were smushed together into one word. The 裸 becomes はだ and the 足 becomes し . You can think of it this way: You were barefoot too long, and because of this, you don't have feet anymore, though you had ashi ( はだし ) at one point in the past.

sentences.japanese: 水虫になりたくないなら、スリッパを裸足で履かない方がいいですよ。
sentences.english: You shouldn’t wear slippers barefoot if you don’t want to get athlete’s foot.

meaningMnemonic: Your torso body is the body area that's your torso. It's your body and trunk and torso , depending on what kind of body you have.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 君は今までみた中で一番胴体が長いよ。
sentences.english: You have the longest torso I’ve ever seen.

meaningMnemonic: If you insert a picture into a book, it becomes a book illustration .
readingMnemonic: The reading used for 挿絵 is an exceptional one. Instead of そう it's さし . When you think of a book illustration , think of an illustration of a sash . meaningMnemonic: Who's the person with the car in the palm of their hand? The 車 here actually comes from 電車 (train), so this person is the train conductor . Think about it — the conductor handles things like checking tickets, making announcements, and giving signals to the driver, so everything that happens on the train is quite literally in their hands… er, palms. Note that these days, even many Japanese people get the 車掌 mixed up with the 運転士 (driver). However, the 車掌 is not the person driving the train — they're more like the train's overall supervisor, in charge of managing passengers and overseeing safety.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.
